subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Common Sense by Thomas Paine
description: A fast breakdown of Common Sense by Thomas Paine for builders.

hook.text: In January 1776, a short pamphlet convinced ordinary colonists that breaking from Britain was necessary.

buildup.text: Thomas Paine wrote Common Sense in plain language anyone could understand, rejecting flowery prose.

discovery.text: Within three months, over one hundred thousand copies circulated among a population of two million.

twist.text: Despite sparking revolution, Paine died in poverty and only six people attended his funeral.

climax.text: Common Sense transformed independence from an elite debate into a populist demand overnight.

punchline.text: Forty-seven pages changed the course of a nation.

quiz.question: Why was Common Sense so influential?
options: It was written in Latin for scholars
It used plain language that ordinary colonists could understand
It was endorsed by the British king
